title: the my
titleRu: Артикль и my вместе не ставят
rule: Do not put a or the before my, your, his, her, our or their. Say my city, not the my city.
ruleRu: Перед my, your, his, her, our, their артикль не ставят. My city, не the my city.
exampleOk: I ride my bike in my city.
exampleBad: I ride my bike at the my city.
l1Trap: Артикль и «мой» ставят вместе: the my city.

title: a or an
rule: Use an before a vowel sound and a before a consonant sound. Listen to the sound, not the letter: an hour, a university.
ruleRu: An ставят перед гласным звуком, a — перед согласным. Слушайте звук, не букву: an hour, a university.
exampleOk: She ate an apple and a sandwich.
exampleBad: She ate a apple and an sandwich.
l1Trap: В русском нет этой пары, поэтому артикль часто пропускают или выбирают по букве: a hour.

title: a with jobs
rule: Use a or an before a job or role in the singular: She is a doctor. Do not say She is doctor.
ruleRu: Перед профессией в единственном числе нужен a или an: She is a doctor. Нельзя She is doctor.
exampleOk: My brother is an engineer.
exampleBad: My brother is engineer.
l1Trap: По-русски говорят «он врач» без артикля, и это переносят в английский.

title: a then the
rule: Use a when you mention a singular countable thing for the first time. Use the when you and the listener already know which one.
ruleRu: Первый раз про одну считаемую вещь — a. Когда уже ясно, о какой именно, — the.
exampleOk: I saw a dog. The dog was hungry.
exampleBad: I saw dog. Dog was hungry.
l1Trap: Русский обходится без артикля, поэтому a и the пропадают оба.

title: no article for things in general
titleRu: Без артикля, когда речь обо всех
rule: Do not use the with a plural or an uncountable noun when you mean things in general. Dogs are friendly. Life is short.
ruleRu: Если речь о виде вообще, the не нужен: Dogs are friendly. Life is short.
exampleOk: I like music.
exampleBad: I like the music.
l1Trap: The ставят на всякий случай перед любым существительным.

title: the when there is only one
rule: Use the when there is only one, or the listener knows which one: the sun, the door, the station.
ruleRu: The, если предмет один на всех или собеседнику и так ясно какой: the sun, the door.
exampleOk: The moon was bright.
exampleBad: A moon was bright.
l1Trap: Уникальные вещи в русском без артикля, и the забывают.

title: school, hospital, work
rule: With no article, school, hospital, church, prison, bed and work mean the activity. The school means the building.
ruleRu: Без артикля school, hospital, work — это занятие. The school — само здание.
exampleOk: She is in hospital. I went to the hospital to visit her.
exampleBad: She is in the hospital because she is ill.
l1Trap: В русском везде «в больнице», поэтому the ставят и когда человек там пациент.

title: articles with places
rule: Most countries have no the: France, Russia. Use the with plurals, unions and rivers: the Netherlands, the USA, the Volga.
ruleRu: Страны обычно без the: France, Russia. The нужно с множественным числом, союзами и реками: the USA, the Volga.
exampleOk: She lives in Russia and visited the United States.
exampleBad: She lives in the Russia and visited United States.
l1Trap: The лепят ко всем странам или, наоборот, забывают у the USA.

title: meals and sports
rule: Meals and sports normally have no article: have breakfast, play football. Use a only for a particular meal: a big breakfast.
ruleRu: Приёмы пищи и виды спорта без артикля: have breakfast, play football. A — только про конкретный: a big breakfast.
exampleOk: We play tennis after lunch.
exampleBad: We play the tennis after the lunch.
l1Trap: The ставят перед lunch и football.

title: play the piano
rule: Use the with musical instruments after play: play the piano. Do not use the with sports: play football.
ruleRu: С инструментом — play the piano. Со спортом артикля нет: play football.
exampleOk: She plays the guitar but she doesn't play chess.
exampleBad: She plays guitar but she plays the chess.
l1Trap: Оба случая уравнивают: либо the везде, либо нигде.

title: plural -s
rule: Add -s for more than one regular noun. After a number greater than one, the noun is plural: two books, not two book.
ruleRu: Если предметов больше одного, у обычного существительного есть -s: two books, не two book.
exampleOk: I have three sisters.
exampleBad: I have three sister.
l1Trap: После числительного в русском форма часто как единственное, и -s забывают.

title: irregular plurals
rule: Some nouns do not take -s: child/children, man/men, woman/women, person/people, foot/feet, tooth/teeth, mouse/mice.
ruleRu: Не все слова образуют множественное через -s: child — children, person — people, tooth — teeth.
exampleOk: There were three children and two women.
exampleBad: There were three childs and two womans.
l1Trap: К неправильным словам всё равно прибавляют -s: childs, peoples.

title: people are
rule: People means more than one person and takes a plural verb: people are, not people is. Peoples means nations.
ruleRu: People значит «люди» и требует глагол во множественном: people are. Peoples — это народы.
exampleOk: People are waiting outside.
exampleBad: People is waiting outside.
l1Trap: People выглядит как единственное число, и к нему ставят is.

title: countable and uncountable
rule: Uncountable nouns have no plural and no a: information, advice, money, furniture, luggage, homework, news. Use a piece of when you need one item.
ruleRu: Information, advice, money, furniture, news не имеют множественного и не берутся с a. Один кусок — a piece of advice.
exampleOk: She gave me a piece of advice.
exampleBad: She gave me an advice.
l1Trap: По-русски «совет» и «информация» считаются, поэтому говорят an advice.

title: news is
rule: News is uncountable and takes a singular verb, even though it ends in -s: the news is good.
ruleRu: News — несчитаемое и с глаголом в единственном, хотя на конце -s: the news is good.
exampleOk: The news is surprising.
exampleBad: The news are surprising.
l1Trap: Из-за -s слово принимают за множественное, как «новости».

title: much and many
rule: Many is for countable plurals: many books. Much is for uncountables: much time. In positive sentences, a lot of is more natural for both.
ruleRu: Many — с тем, что можно посчитать: many books. Much — с тем, что нельзя: much time. В обычной фразе чаще a lot of.
exampleOk: There isn't much time, but there are many questions.
exampleBad: There isn't many time, but there are much questions.
l1Trap: Оба слова соответствуют «много», и их путают местами.

title: some and any
rule: Some is normal in positive sentences and in offers. Any is normal in questions and negatives. Would you like some tea? I don't want any sugar.
ruleRu: Some — в утверждениях и когда что-то предлагают. Any — в вопросах и отрицаниях.
exampleOk: Would you like some tea? I don't want any sugar.
exampleBad: Would you like any tea? I don't want some sugar.
l1Trap: В русском и там и там «какой-нибудь», поэтому some и any ставят наугад.

title: a few and a little
rule: A few is a small number of countable things. A little is a small amount of an uncountable thing. Both mean some, and that is enough.
ruleRu: A few — немного штук. A little — немного массы. Оба значат «немного, и этого хватает».
exampleOk: I have a few friends and a little free time.
exampleBad: I have a little friends and a few free time.
l1Trap: «Немного» одно на оба случая, поэтому a few time и a little friends.

title: few and little without a
rule: Few and little without a mean almost none, and that is a problem. A few and a little mean some.
ruleRu: Few и little без a — «почти нет, и это плохо». A few и a little — «немного есть».
exampleOk: Few people came, so we cancelled. A few people stayed to help.
exampleBad: A few people came, so the room was empty.
l1Trap: Артикль a кажется необязательным, и смысл меняется на противоположный.

title: there is and there are
rule: There is for one thing, there are for more than one. The verb agrees with the first noun.
ruleRu: There is — один предмет, there are — несколько. Глагол согласуется с первым существительным.
exampleOk: There are two windows in the room.
exampleBad: There is two windows in the room.
l1Trap: «Есть» не меняется, поэтому there is ставят и перед множественным.

title: this, that, these, those
rule: This and that are singular. These and those are plural. This and these are near, that and those are far.
ruleRu: This и that — один предмет. These и those — много. This и these близко, that и those далеко.
exampleOk: These shoes are new. That shop is far.
exampleBad: This shoes are new. Those shop is far.
l1Trap: This оставляют и перед множественным: this books.

title: possessive 's
rule: For people and animals, add 's: Anna's book. For a plural ending in -s, add only the apostrophe: the students' room.
ruleRu: У людей и животных — 's: Anna's book. Если множественное уже на -s, апостроф без второй s: the students' room.
exampleOk: This is my sister's phone.
exampleBad: This is the phone of my sister's.
l1Trap: Вместо 's строят the book of Anna или ставят s без апострофа.

title: noun before noun stays singular
rule: A noun used as a description stays singular: a two-hour trip, a shoe shop. Not a two-hours trip.
ruleRu: Существительное в роли определения остаётся в единственном: a two-hour trip, a shoe shop. Не two-hours.
exampleOk: It was a three-day trip.
exampleBad: It was a three-days trip.
l1Trap: Число ставят и в определение: three-days, shoes shop.

title: I and me
rule: I, he, she, we, they are subjects. Me, him, her, us, them come after a verb or preposition.
ruleRu: I, he, she, we, they — подлежащие. Me, him, her, us, them — после глагола и предлога.
exampleOk: Anna and I went home. She called me.
exampleBad: Me and Anna went home. She called I.
l1Trap: Me and ставят в подлежащее, либо I оставляют после глагола.

title: my and mine
rule: My, your, his, her, our, their stand before a noun. Mine, yours, hers, ours, theirs stand alone.
ruleRu: My, your, his, her стоят перед существительным. Mine, yours, hers — сами по себе.
exampleOk: This is my bag. That one is mine.
exampleBad: This is mine bag. That one is my.
l1Trap: My и mine оба значат «мой», и их меняют местами.

title: its and it's
rule: It's means it is or it has. Its is possessive and has no apostrophe. The cat ate its food. It's hungry.
ruleRu: It's = it is или it has. Its — «его/её» про предмет, без апострофа.
exampleOk: It's cold and the dog wants its blanket.
exampleBad: Its cold and the dog wants it's blanket.
l1Trap: Апостроф ставят по аналогии с Ivan's, и it's становится «его».

title: capital I
rule: The pronoun I is always a capital letter, even in the middle of a sentence. Other pronouns are not.
ruleRu: Местоимение I всегда пишется большой буквой, даже в середине фразы.
exampleOk: My sister and I live here.
exampleBad: My sister and i live here.
l1Trap: В русском «я» не особое, и i пишут строчной.

title: myself, yourself
rule: Use myself, yourself, himself, herself, ourselves, themselves when the subject and the object are the same person. Do not use myself as a polite subject.
ruleRu: Myself, yourself, himself и остальные — когда подлежащее и дополнение один человек. Вместо I их не ставят.
exampleOk: I taught myself to cook.
exampleBad: My friend and myself taught us to cook.
l1Trap: Myself кажется вежливее, чем I, и его ставят в подлежащее.

title: whose
rule: Whose asks about an owner. Who's means who is. Whose bag is this?
ruleRu: Whose спрашивает «чей». Who's значит who is.
exampleOk: Whose keys are these?
exampleBad: Who's keys are these?
l1Trap: Who's пишут вместо whose, потому что звучат одинаково.
